# SOLID STATE — H2A Threshold Calibration

**Measurements only.** Generated by the headless engine from
`content/balance/SOLID_STATE_H2A_THRESHOLD_CALIBRATION_PLAN_v0.1.json`.

Compare current authored FIX gates against retained LOW/MID/HIGH reversible profiles after the first human H2A playtest. Add stat-drift, event-frequency, housing, low-stat risk, and faction-chain telemetry. Do not freeze a profile automatically.

No threshold profile is selected or frozen here. Canonical FIX gates are never edited: LOW/MID/HIGH are applied through the retained reversible rewrite in `src/sim/experiments.ts`, in memory only. The written recommendation lives in [`docs/H2A_THRESHOLD_CALIBRATION_FINDINGS.md`](../docs/H2A_THRESHOLD_CALIBRATION_FINDINGS.md); decisions stay in [`docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`](../docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md). This file is regenerated on every run.

### Method notes

- CURRENT_AUTHORED is the canonical corpus with no threshold rewrite at all. The Phase 1.1 `ORIGINAL_REFERENCE` profile is deliberately NOT used as the control: canonical gates changed after Phase 1.1, so that arm is historical rather than current.
- LOW/MID/HIGH use the retained reversible rewrite in `src/sim/experiments.ts`, which rewrites assigned event FIX gates and the validity conditions of schedules pointing at them, in memory only. Canonical event JSON is never written.
- Every arm uses the same base seed. A rewritten arm carries a derived content fingerprint, and the run seed is `contentVersion:seed`, so the arms are independent samples of the same sampling design rather than a paired comparison. This matches the retained Phase 1.1 experiment behaviour; at these run counts the sampling error on a rate near 50% is roughly ±0.9pp.
- Species are stratified equally, so a species roll cannot drift between arms.
- ARCHETYPE_SET priorities are read verbatim from the retained Phase 1.1 experiment matrix. No new archetype is invented and no allocation comparison is run.
- Visible stats are unclamped in the canonical balance constants, and this run adds no clamp and changes no stat effect.

Deliberately **not** run in this task (harness retained, not retired):

- family-weight A/B
- allocation policy comparison
- T1027 sensitivity sweep
- T1023 targeted comparison
- neutral-Human manifestation diagnostic

All omitted harnesses remain retained for H2B or future relevant regression work.

## 4. Visible-stat telemetry

Fixed-age snapshots are taken **entering** that age and include only runs still active then; the active count is the denominator on every row. `start` is the post-setup baseline and is the reference for drift. Visible stats are unclamped in the canonical balance constants and nothing here clamps them.

## 7. Low-stat conditional risk

Person-year analysis from age 18. Each observed year is classified by the stat value **entering** that year, then followed forward. A person-year counts toward a horizon only when its follow-up is complete: the run either reached an ending, or was still being simulated at `age + horizon`. Person-years censored by the diagnostic maximum age are dropped rather than counted as "no event". Commitment and faction-COMMITTED probabilities are conditioned on that outcome not having happened yet, so their denominators differ.

**This is correlation, not causation, and no danger weighting is implemented.**

## 8. Faction-chain legibility

Attribution uses canonical `factionIds` / `factionInteraction` metadata. A **personalized touchpoint** is an event addressed to the player by that faction — interaction `contact`, `personal` or `climax`. News bulletins and lore fallback are world texture and are excluded. "First disposition" is the first lifecycle move after CONTACTED; "escalation after ENGAGED" is any later personalized touchpoint; "climax after COMMITTED" is a `climax` event at or after the COMMITTED transition.

## 9. Review-band check

Mechanical comparison against the review bands stated in the calibration plan and review guide. These are **review bands, not final game targets**, and a flag is a discussion point, not a rejection. Nothing here selects a profile.

| Arm | Flags |
|---|---|
| **CURRENT_AUTHORED** | completion 25.7% below the 45–70% review band; commitment 37.6% below the 45–70% review band; mean commitment age 35.7 above the early-30s preference; largest ending bucket is 65+, not 25-34; 65+ still holds 50.8% of endings; 1 guardrail failure(s) |
| **LOW** | completion 42.5% below the 45–70% review band; mean commitment age 35.3 above the early-30s preference; largest ending bucket is 35-44, not 25-34; 1 guardrail failure(s) |
| **MID** | completion 33.1% below the 45–70% review band; mean commitment age 35.4 above the early-30s preference; largest ending bucket is 35-44, not 25-34; 1 guardrail failure(s) |
| **HIGH** | completion 24.3% below the 45–70% review band; commitment 39.8% below the 45–70% review band; mean commitment age 35.4 above the early-30s preference; largest ending bucket is 35-44, not 25-34; 1 guardrail failure(s) |

The written recommendation — which arm, if any, is plausible as a provisional H2A profile, and the material/faction/stat tradeoffs — is in [`docs/H2A_THRESHOLD_CALIBRATION_FINDINGS.md`](../docs/H2A_THRESHOLD_CALIBRATION_FINDINGS.md). It is analysis only: no profile is written into content, no threshold is interpolated, and Q-27 stays open until design reviews this calibration.

## 10. Required core metrics checklist

- completion and nonterminal rate
- ending count per 1000 runs
- ending-age bucket counts, share of all runs, and share of completed runs
- mean/median/p10/p90 ending age
- ending coverage and ending ID distribution
- ending counts by route family and faction
- material commitment rate
- mean/median material commitment age
- mean FIX at commitment and ending
- final material distribution and material guardrails
- route climax rates
- schedule expiry/displacement/collision metrics
- generic fallback and lore fallback by age band
- pre-25 correctness counters
- faction correctness counters
